implemented: production task snapshots group eligible top-level windows by authoritative application identity
single-window buttons retain activate, minimize, and restore behavior while multi-window buttons open an owned GPUI flyout
flyout cards are rebuilt from a fresh authoritative snapshot and stale group members are omitted
DWM composition and live-HWND preview capability is revalidated within the 500 millisecond admission budget
admitted source windows are registered with DwmRegisterThumbnail, updated to the GPUI card's DPI-scaled client rectangle, and unregistered by an owning Drop lease
title/state fallback remains visible when live preview is unavailable
pointer activation and close plus keyboard Left, Right, Enter, Delete, and Escape share typed FlyoutAction routes
activation, restore, and WM_CLOSE are admitted only after the target HWND is revalidated
flyout dialog, card, close-button, accessible labels, focus order, and visible focus state are wired
group and flyout windows use per-monitor logical placement above the taskbar
right-clicking a production task opens an owned accessible Jump List populated by the isolated provider host from bounded Windows Recent items and validated application tasks
Jump List pin or unpin and close-all commands remain local, revalidate HWNDs, atomically persist pin order, and refresh task ordering
normal, indeterminate, paused, error, badge, and attention overlays have independent production render paths
rows, pin order, combine-groups, labels, preview enablement, and multi-monitor preferences load from the versioned settings store and alter production layout/behavior
remaining_external_integration: legacy third-party ITaskbarList3 progress and overlay calls still target the registered Windows taskband COM service; SuperDesktop renders all overlay states but a compatibility COM ingress requires a separately approved Windows shell-registration boundary
capture a physical shell-mode DWM thumbnail screenshot and timing artifact on the Windows 10 evidence machine
